why: The contract between the two ring comparators. test_ring.py asserts that the Python one returns
exactly the errors this table records, and test-ring.mjs asserts the same of the JavaScript one,
so a case added here constrains both implementations.
The ring is rotation-insensitive and orientation-SENSITIVE. That asymmetry is the whole point:
the engine renormalises every reported surface to an upper-left start, so a rotation carries no
information, while a reversal is exactly the difference the clockwise entry clause exists to
produce. A comparator that also minimised over the reversal would pass a model resolved inside
out, and checks/geometry-vertices/check.md would be asserting something it does not check.
Coordinates are metres. The base ring is a 4 m by 3 m rectangle in the y = 0 plane, so its
sides are 3 and 4 and its diagonal is 5, and every expected error below can be read off by hand.

cases.name: identical
cases.note: the trivial case, present so a comparator that always returns zero is not the only thing this table forbids

cases.name: rotated by one
cases.note: the same ring starting elsewhere. THIS MUST PASS: it is what the engine's renormalisation produces

cases.name: reversed
cases.note: THIS MUST FAIL. The same four vertices wound the other way, best-aligned at 3 m, which is the rectangle's short side

cases.name: reversed and rotated
cases.note: a reversal is still a reversal after any rotation, so rotating one cannot rescue it

cases.name: displaced within tolerance
cases.note: 3 mm, inside the half-of-the-last-printed-place the report can express

cases.name: displaced beyond tolerance
cases.note: 1 cm, which the report would have printed

cases.name: one vertex out
cases.note: the error is the WORST vertex and not the mean, so one bad corner cannot be averaged away by three good ones

cases.name: triangle rotated
cases.note: rings are not all four-sided; the corpus holds 3-sided and 4-sided surfaces and the format permits more

rejected.name: different lengths
rejected.note: a disagreement about the surface rather than about where it is. Comparing the three against any three of the four would report a small error for a missing corner

rejected.name: empty
rejected.note: an empty ring has no error to report, and returning zero for it would make a surface with no vertices agree with everything
